test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A shaft with a basic size of 40 mm has a clearance allowance of 0.06 mm. What is the design size of the shaft?
solution:
**Concept**

 
• **Basic Size:** It is the size of a part to which limits of size are applied. It is the same for both the hole and the shaft in a mating pair.
 
• **Allowance:** It is the intentional difference between the maximum material limits of mating parts. It represents the minimum clearance or maximum interference.
 
• **Clearance Allowance:** In a clearance fit, the shaft is always smaller than the hole. To provide a clearance allowance, the shaft size must be reduced from the basic size (assuming the hole is at basic size).
